summary: 1. A new mining meeting note (30-Aug) surfaces a live production constraint: the primary crusher's hammer has a flat chisel head instead of a tapered/pointed one, and can't break rock effectively. 2. Combined with MG feed running 70-90% rock, the grizzly is choking on oversize (must be under 500mm) and the crusher group has been reporting delays for three days. 3. Fix identified — swap to a tapered/stubbed chisel, action assigned to Jack Reabow — with a feed workaround in the meantime (high-grade first to open the area, then blend low-grade with MG1 as pressure drops). 2. 4. The same meeting details Stage 4 / level 171 access sequencing (mine top-down to connect to 171, since starting from 740 wasn't possible), the 263 blast down to its last 1-2 truck trips, a dozer tipping-technique correction, and an unresolved evacuation-point discrepancy between the mapped switchback 3 point and a supervisor's verbal guidance to park at the pre-slip point instead. 3. 5.
